findings.title: Slots on a day with two or more date-override ranges are all rejected, because `find` rejects a slot when any same-day override does not contain it
findings.description: `dateOverrides.find` returns truthy for any same-day override that ends before the slot starts (lines 117-122) or starts before the slot ends (line 123-124). The caller then returns `false` for the slot (lines 128-130). The callback never asks whether some override contains the slot. Take two same-day ranges, A 09:00–10:00 IST and B 14:00–18:00 IST. A 14:00 IST slot is after A, so A's callback returns true at line 123 and the slot is rejected. A 09:00 IST slot is before B, so B's callback returns true at line 118 and it is rejected too. `getUserAvailability` (`packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:215-224`) emits one entry per override row, so multi-range overrides reach this function as separate entries.

findings.title: Slots inside a date-override window skip the busy-time check and can be double-booked
findings.description: When any same-day override exists and the slot is not rejected, `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. `lib/slots.ts:206-246` drops the weekly hours on override days and emits only slots inside the override window, so every slot on such a day takes this early return. Calendar busy times (`schedule.busy`, spread into the call at lines 488-493) and existing bookings are never consulted. Example: override 14:00–18:00 IST with a calendar event 15:00–16:00 IST. The 15:00 IST slot (09:30Z) passes at line 134 and is offered. Before this change the busy check ran for every slot.

findings.title: A day with two or more working-hour blocks rejects every slot on that day
findings.description: `workingHours.find` returns truthy if any block on the slot's weekday does not contain the slot (lines 140-146). For a split day, 09:30–12:00 and 14:00–18:00 IST, `getWorkingHours` (`packages/lib/availability.ts:76-124`) produces UTC blocks `[240,390]` and `[510,750]`. A 04:00Z slot is outside the second block (`240 < 510`), and an 08:30Z slot is outside the first (`510 > 390`). Each is rejected at line 150. The per-user `workingHours` reach this check unchanged via `...schedule` (lines 488-493).

findings.title: Overrides whose shifted times cross midnight keep the wrong day, so a New York Monday 22:00–23:30 override appears on London Monday at 03:00
findings.description: The offset `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` (line 214) is added to the wall-clock minutes. The result is then reduced with `.hour()*60 + .minute()` (lines 219-223), which discards the day rollover. The day is still chosen by the unshifted start in the filter at lines 206-208. Trace: override labeled Mon 22:00Z, organizer offset −300, invitee London 0. Offset is +300, so startTime is 03:00 (180) and endTime is 04:30 (270). The filter keeps it for London Monday, so the slot shows Monday 03:00–04:30 London. The real instant is Tuesday 03:00–04:30 London. The pre-change `getUTCHours` code also put it on the wrong day, so this is not a regression, but the new conversion still yields the wrong day.

findings.title: The override day match formats one side in server-local time and the other in UTC, so overrides near UTC midnight are rejected when the process timezone is not UTC
findings.description: `dayjs(date.start)` at line 110 has no `.utc()` or `.tz()`, so `.format()` uses the process timezone. `slotStartTime` (line 100) is UTC, and line 111 formats it in UTC. On a server in America/New_York, an override that starts at 01:00Z on day D formats as D−1 and never matches a slot on D. `dateOverrideExist` stays false, the slot falls through to the working-hours check (lines 138-151), and it is rejected when the user's hours start later. Example: an override at 06:30 IST with hours from 09:30 IST. On a UTC server the same slot is accepted.
